guard: the membership feed refuses an un-re-signed rw generation by GENERATION, not by envelope bytes
why: The refusal is a two-conjunct predicate, and a mutation against the DELAY conjunct can report a clean
kill while the equality conjunct stays entirely ungraded. This fixture flips the equality conjunct
back to the byte comparison it used to be, so the cell that reddens is the one about generations.
Scenario 5 serves one exact string and stays GREEN under the mutation: byte equality and generation
equality agree there, which is why it could never have caught this.
The sibling cell asserting the refusal MESSAGE cannot grade this either, and is kept for what it
documents rather than for what it discriminates: under the mutation the message still appears, one
1s tick later, once the adopted envelope has become the cached one.

mutations.name: the missed-remint refusal compares envelope bytes again
mutations.expectRed: the refusal keeps the 60s backoff — no 1s re-read of the source (#1563)
mutations.cell: the refusal keeps the 60s backoff — no 1s re-read of the source (#1563)
mutations.note: Exactly the pre-fix line: the tree compiles and scenario 5 still passes, because byte equality and generation equality agree on the one exact string it serves. Graded on the READ COUNT, not on the refusal message: under the mutation the first tick adopts the reformatted read, and the tick 1s later compares bytes-equal and emits the refusal after all - so the message appears either way, one tick late. The 1s re-read is what only happens when the adoption went through.
